newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU farmers lobby attacks proposed price cuts.
newsitem.headline: EU farmers lobby attacks proposed price cuts.

text.p: European farmers on Wednesday attacked proposals to cut dairy, cereals and beef intervention prices by between 10 and 30 percent and provide only partial compensation for income losses.
The proposals, presented to the European Parliament on Wednesday, are aimed at making farmers more competitive and preparing for EU enlargement eastwards.

"The proposals are unacceptable as they stand. Their implementation would have very damaging consequences for the future of farmers and their families...," said Risto Volanen, the Finnish Secretary General of COPA, the EU farmers' lobby.
Volanen said in a statement that the cuts would be very damaging, hitting farm jobs and threatening the viability of vast rural areas.
"They would put at risk the existence of certain sectors of the production and could lead to the renationalisation of the CAP (Common Agricultural Policy) which is totally unacceptable," he added.
On Friday, COPA's French President told a news conference in Brussels that if the proposals were implemented they would have a catastrophic impact on farmers' revenues.
